To the Fields of Midori Island
Take the train to Midori Island with Mr. Tanaka: buy the ticket, watch the sea from the window, and learn to till, sow and water in his grandmother's field.
Meet Mr. Tanaka
Buy a ticket at Hibari Station
Arrive at Midori Island
Receive Grandma's field
Hello. I hear you went to the Game Center with Kim. Was it fun?
Yes, it was a lot of fun.
Hello. Your Japanese has really improved lately.
Oh no, I still have a long way to go.
Yes, I'm good.
Haha, confident! In Japan many people say 「まだまだです」 (still a long way to go).
Actually, my grandmother has a field on Midori Island. Would you like to come with me this weekend?
I'd love to go! How do we get there?
Yes, I'll go.
What is a 'hatake'?
A hatake is a place where you grow vegetables. Tomatoes, carrots and so on.
We'll take the train. From Hibari Station to Midori Island it's about an hour. Can you buy a ticket by yourself?
Yes, Mr. Kimura taught me.
It's a little difficult.
No problem. Let's go together. I'll be right next to you.
The weekend, Hibari Station. You look for the 「みどり島」 button on the ticket machine.
To Midori Island it's 650 yen. How much will you put in?
I'll put in 650 yen.
I'll put in 560 yen.
Oops, that's not enough. Six hundred, fifty. It's 650 yen.
The train starts moving. Outside the window you can see the blue sea.
You can see the sea, can't you. What can you see?
I can see the sea and a small island.
I look at the sea.
That's right. But here we say 「海が見えます」 (I can see the sea).
You've arrived at Midori Island. In front of the station there are wide fields.
Grandma is watering the field right now. Let's sow some seeds too.
Okay. What do we do first?
Do we eat the seeds?
Haha, we don't eat seeds. We 「まきます」 (sow) them into the soil.
First, you till the soil with a hoe. Next, you sow the seeds, and finally you water them.
What do we do last?
We water them.
We sow the seeds.
That's the next step. First, till. Next, sow. And last…?
Grandma says, “You can use this field.” It's your field now!
Really? Thank you so much! I'll take good care of it.
Thanks.
Today's points: ~de ikimasu (go by), ~ga miemasu (can see), mazu / tsugi ni / saigo ni (in order), ~te mo ii (you may). Your field on the island is ready!
